summary.headline: Radiant Q2 FY27: standalone EBITDA margin fell to 7.62% from 15.2% on manpower cost surge; 12-15% price hikes to hit from Q4.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue grew 7.52% YoY while cash volume was flat at INR 0.41 trillion in a lean quarter. Manpower costs (about 70% of total cost) rose sharply on minimum wage revisions and shortage of licensed gunmen, cutting standalone EBITDA margin to 7.62% from 15.2%. Management has secured price revisions of 12-15% from most clients, mainly banks, with the effect expected from Q4 FY27. Consolidated revenue was INR 1.12 billion (+4.4%), with consolidated EBITDA margin at 6.8% versus 13.1%, and Radiant Acemoney reached near-EBITDA breakeven. Net debt is nil.

segments.name: Retail cash management (standalone)
segments.commentary: Cash handled INR 0.41 trillion, flat YoY; retail cash management grew 6.2%, with BFSI and organised retail driving growth and railways, petroleum and e-commerce sluggish. Direct clients were 19.2% of revenue (18.4% in Q1, 15.7% a year ago).

segments.name: Radiant Valuable Logistics (RVL)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 29.9 million, up 35% QoQ, but still loss-making; management targets positive EBITDA within FY27 after inducting a new business development and load-factor team.

segments.name: Radiant Acemoney (fintech subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue turned in a healthy recovery and EBITDA was near breakeven in Q2. Network of close to 20,000 BCs, 21,000 sound boxes deployed in the quarter, about INR 200 crore transaction volume; target of 50,000+ sound boxes in FY27; MOUs signed with two small finance banks, one urban bank and some NBFCs.

guidance_outlook: Price revisions of 12-15% across most clients, mostly banks; most to be implemented by December 2026, with some from 1 November; impact visible from Q4 FY27 and steadier in FY28.

Management expects healthy profitability improvement in the remaining FY27 quarters from price hikes, cost reduction using AI/technology in route management, banking, recon and billing, and turnaround at RVL and Acemoney.
RVL and Acemoney expected to turn positive on EBITDA and PAT in FY27; RVL profitability targeted by end of FY27.
Long-term aspiration: restore profitability to IPO-time levels and achieve mid-teens revenue growth.
No meaningful capex planned; vans mostly leased. Management is weighing a share buyback suggestion but has not committed; dividend retained for now.
capex_capacity: Serviced 79,374 points across 15,165 pin codes and 9,217 locations; point coverage up 5% YoY.
Management says industry handles under 2 lakh points against about 2 crore retail outlets in India; Radiant targets about 40-45% share of the retail cash management market.
Capex minimal: vans leased and other capex described as miniscule; subsidiary spend is self-liquidating sound box inventory, not capex.
demand_pricing: Price revisions of 12-15% negotiated jointly with peers via the industry association and banks; banks gave interim increases on running contracts. Public sector bank clients asked Radiant to take up pricing with their end customers, which will take longer.
Pricing is broadly similar across service providers for a given bank; direct-client pricing follows the same mechanism. Around 80% of business comes through banks, 20% direct.
No fuel pass-through exists. Gunman shortage is specific to several southern states; no clear timeline for easing.
Value proposition cited: daily pickup for INR 1 lakh/day starts at about INR 2,500 per month (under INR 100 per visit), about 20-25 bps of cash volume against about 200 bps MDR on credit cards.
Management says the core business has been growing 5-7% and expects revenue growth to recover; current cash volume is about INR 1.6 lakh crore annually, flat YoY.
Competitive context: management declined to compare with the industry leader's margins, citing lack of disclosure.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Radiant's margins in single digits when the industry leader holds mid-20s margins, and can the 12-15% price hike restore the standalone margin to about 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to compare with peers and said it could not give a precise margin number; start dates vary by bank, but the improvement will be 'definite' and significant from Q4, with the 20-21% level not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the receivables jump as of 30 September a new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it was one-time: September collections were slightly lower, and the amounts were collected in the first week of October, with good collections in October.

qa_highlights.question: What levers beyond price hikes can restore margins toward IPO-era levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Four drivers: price hikes (main), arresting RVL and Acemoney losses, technology-led cost reduction on manpower (70% of cost), and longer-term direct-client growth. Management said the 5-7% top-line growth of recent years should be an aberration.

qa_highlights.question: Will UPI/MDR charges after Diwali help cash volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: October performance was very healthy, helped by the festive season. Management said higher digital volumes could eventually lift cash volumes but gave no quantified impact.

qa_highlights.question: Will the buyback suggestion be considered given net cash of above INR 150 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a buyback would need to be substantial to matter, shareholders favour dividends, and the board would go with majority opinion and advice from financial advisers; no decision taken.

qa_highlights.question: Does the price hike apply to retail and bank contracts, and is any competitor undercutting?
qa_highlights.answer: Most hikes are from banks via interim escalations on running contracts; management said the increase was an industry-wide joint decision and no peer is undercutting.

qa_highlights.question: Do elections affect cash movement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said elections have no material impact on cash movement, with clearances from the Election Commission and local authorities and certificates carried in vans.

risks_watch: Recovery depends on the 12-15% price hikes being fully implemented by December; public sector bank pricing is still pending and may take longer.
Further manpower cost inflation (minimum wage revisions, gunman shortage in southern states) could erode price gains; no fuel pass-through exists.
Flat cash volume (INR 0.41 trillion) and sluggish railways, petroleum and e-commerce segments; points growth relies on new direct clients.
RVL remains loss-making with a lengthening breakeven timeline; Acemoney is near EBITDA breakeven but depends on new bank and NBFC mandates.
Reported PAT margin of 3.5% and ROCE of 5.4% are weak; watch Q3 and Q4 FY27 for margin recovery.
summary.management_tone: Confident about recovery but defensive on the quarter: the CMD called the performance 'underwhelming' while saying 'the worst is behind us'. Management was evasive on peer comparisons and on quantifying margin recovery.
key_quotes: The overall performance for the quarter has been underwhelming.
However, the management is confident that the worst is behind us, and the coming quarters will report much healthier numbers.
We had the least gross cash losses in this quarter since our listing at INR 1 million.
